indicators.note: done roughly, the letters of the word veers are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for north on a compass

explanation.surface: A river swings off its course towards the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veers' reads as the river's motion, but is the raw material. The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and western England.
explanation.definitionFit: Named watercourse: the longest river in Great Britain, running into the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Missile launcher fitted to aircraft carriers

definitions.text: Missile launcher fitted to aircraft carriers

parts.words: Missile launcher fitted to aircraft carriers
parts.note: the schoolboy's stone-flinging sling and the steam device that hurls jets off a carrier deck share one name

explanation.surface: A naval weapons system installed aboard aircraft carriers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a missile battery; the device on a carrier launches aircraft, and the same word is the child's slingshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a hand-held sling for stones and the deck mechanism that propels planes into flight bear this name.

clue.text: A point that was put on record

definitions.meaning: a sharp slender tip, as on a sewing tool
the stylus lowered onto a vinyl disc on an old gramophone

explanation.definitionFit: Sewing implement with a sharp tip, and also the stylus that sat in the groove of a gramophone disc.

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned term for a cad, a man beyond the social pale
a horse that leaps well over fences, one that bounds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outsider' looks like a racing long shot, matching the steeplechase; here it means a cad, a dated British word for an ill-mannered man.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang for a dishonourable man, and jocularly a horse that jumps well.

clue.text: Where a shopkeeper needs to carry identification

definitions.text: Where a shopkeeper needs to carry identification

parts.words: Where a shopkeeper needs to carry identification
parts.note: the board above a shop front carries the business name, identifying the shop

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is asked where to keep an ID card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry identification' suggests a person showing papers; it is the signboard over the shopfront that bears the trading name.
explanation.definitionFit: Name board above a shop front displaying the business title.

indicators.note: letters gone astray wander out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Lost post leads customers to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges MAILSENT. 'complaints' looks like customer grievances but means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: minor illnesses or disorders are called complaints.

parts.note: the French particle 'de' as in noble surnames makes a Franco version of the name
David Cameron, British prime minister 2010-2016

explanation.surface: Stories about a French-English prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco' looks like the Spanish dictator but signals French: DE as in 'de Gaulle' prefixed to CAMERON, then PM.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's fourteenth-century compilation of a hundred stories told by young Florentines.

clue.text: Blame one laid on head of Dean Swift

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Dean

explanation.surface: Blame is placed on Dean Swift, the satirist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean Swift' is Jonathan Swift, Dean of St Patrick's; here 'Swift' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe something very fast.

clue.text: Phone about disruption of trade causing delay

indicators.note: the phone word goes about, surrounding, the other piece

parts.note: to ring is to phone someone

indicators.note: disruption throws the letters of trade out of order

explanation.surface: A telephone call about a trade stoppage holds things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing delay' is the definition; 'Phone' is a verb giving the outer piece, and the trade dispute is only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Slowing down or holding back progress means causing a delay.

clue.text: Swindle quietly put together by rogue

parts.note: a scam is a swindle
P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

explanation.surface: A con trick is quietly organised by a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mischievous rascal or scallywag.

clue.text: Record the same note twice — it's sharp

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the note is written two times in a row

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A musician records one note twice and finds it sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' suggests a pitch; it is a pointed fencing sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing sword with a pointed blade, so a weapon with an edge to it.

parts.note: the close is the end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: Something nearby along a river or stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brook' looks like a stream to match 'river', but is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to brook something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Frank, ensnared in sex scandal, reveals all

indicators.note: the candid word is trapped inside the other piece
a scandal is a mess, so the word sex is thrown into disorder

parts.note: plain speaking is frank speaking

explanation.surface: An honest person caught up in a sex scandal tells everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man caught in the scandal, but means candid; 'reveals all' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Makes things clear, setting out every detail plainly.

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one
a stake is the amount put up in betting

explanation.surface: A betting slip at odds of a thousand to one.
explanation.walkthrough: '1,000-1' looks like long odds; it is M and I. 'betting slip' is split: STAKE then the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an error or blunder.

clue.text: Ex-US president takes round new British PM

indicators.note: the president's name takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower

indicators.note: making it new rearranges the letters of round

explanation.surface: A former American president hosts a new British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British PM' looks like a current leader, but the Iron Duke was Wellington, victor at Waterloo, who later became prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname of the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo, who served as prime minister.

definitions.meaning: in snooker or billiards, balls that touch lightly are said to do this
a greeting given with the lips

explanation.walkthrough: 'oral' suggests speech, but the greeting is made with the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lips pressed in affection, and the cue-sports term for balls brushing together.

definitions.meaning: a defeat or reversal of fortune
the back or opposite face of a coin or page

explanation.definitionFit: Means both a misfortune or defeat and the back face of something.

clue.text: Girl holds chap up in Denmark

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the other piece inside

parts.note: Elsie is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A girl lifts a man up while in Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RON into NOR, which ELSIE 'holds'. Elsinore is the Danish castle town of Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Port town on the Danish coast, setting of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

parts.note: the mythical beast holding up the shield on the British coat of arms, opposite the lion

explanation.surface: A wonderful backer of the monarchy's military forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means legendary, not marvellous; 'arms' is heraldry, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythical horned horse that stands as a heraldic supporter on the royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Suspect hijinks for the departing prodigal?

definitions.meaning: the prodigal son of the parable as he leaves home

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as a leaving son, the prodigal of Luke's parable.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady or questionable activities, and punningly the son as he leaves.

definitions.meaning: something that grows: a stinging weed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing anger' reads as rising fury; split it into a plant and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinging weed found in gardens, and a verb meaning to irritate.

indicators.note: moving the letters of side shifts them into another order

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A good man is told to stop moving to the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges SIDE into DESI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cease or refrain from doing something.

parts.note: 'got up' means dressed, not rose from bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up smartly' suggests rising briskly; 'got up' is dressed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes clothing that is elegant or formal, as worn on smart occasions.

clue.text: Sent us out at the end of the day

indicators.note: out means the letters of the phrase are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone sent us away at close of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SENTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening moment when the sun goes down, closing daylight.

clue.text: Woman who has to polish hard

parts.note: to edit text is to polish it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A woman who has to polish things vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard' looks like an adverb on polishing, but gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's first name.

definitions.meaning: a place hidden behind screens, shielded from view

explanation.walkthrough: 'cover-up' hints at scandal; it is a literal shielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Film presentation, and the act of shielding something from view.

parts.note: nut is slang for head, so its case is the bony shell of the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'nutcase' means a madman in slang; read literally it is the casing of the nut, slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bony structure enclosing the head, slang nut.

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a withdrawn person is reserved

explanation.surface: Someone stayed quiet and kept to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept quiet' looks like one phrase; split it after 'Kept'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: maintained or saved from decay.
